name: client-order-lifecycle-tracking-fulfillment
executionConcern: owned order readback and legal cross-surface fulfillment, tracking, pickup, proof, cancellation/return/exception convergence
objective: Make every client order list/detail/tracking/pickup/delivery/cancellation/return/exception state a privacy-safe projection of one versioned DSH state machine written only by authorized actors and converging after retry, conflict and restart.
truthOwner: DSH owns order, dispatch, custody, pickup, proof and fulfillment operational truth; Partner/Captain/Operator are bounded writers and WLT owns financial consequences.

tasks.objective: Close client-owned order reads, action policy and deep-link authorization
tasks.currentProblem: Order list/tracking screens and notification navigation exist, but guessed IDs, stale action availability or deep links can become security/correctness defects unless each read/action is re-authorized against the current owned order/version.
tasks.requiredChange: Trace client order list/detail/action policy and deep-link targets through shared/generated DSH contracts to order handlers/repositories. Repair actor/object scope, field redaction, version/action policy and canonical reload.
tasks.targetState: The client can enumerate/read only owned orders, sees only server-authorized actions and fields for the current version, and every deep link re-authorizes the owned order before rendering or acting.
tasks.action: Fix DSH order read/action policy owner first, then client order/deep-link presentation and tests.
mustNotChange: Do not authorize from an order ID in a deep link alone.
Do not derive legal actions from status text in the client.
Do not disclose another client's address/location/proof.
Do not use cached order state as final truth after mutation.
acceptanceCriteria: Wrong-actor order IDs are denied or hidden.
Deep links re-authorize the exact target object.
Client action availability matches current server policy/version.
Committed order reload clears stale local action/state after every transition.
tasks.rollback: Revert the focused unit commit or roll forward at DSH while preserving audit/financial lineage; never restore a local order state machine.
tasks.commitBoundary: Owned-order read/action policy plus directly affected client/shared navigation only.

tasks.objective: Close preparation, assignment, custody, tracking, pickup and delivery transitions across writers
tasks.currentProblem: Partner, Captain and operator surfaces can write client-visible fulfillment state; static screens cannot prove one legal versioned transition sequence, idempotent handoff, location privacy or canonical convergence.
tasks.requiredChange: Trace partner preparation, dispatch/assignment, handoff/custody, location, pickup and proof commands through contracts, DSH orders/dispatch/pickup/partnerdelivery and database. Repair authorization, expected version/state, idempotency, proof/custody invariants and affected client readback.
tasks.targetState: All authorized writers advance one DSH order/custody state machine; stale/forbidden/duplicate transitions fail safely; tracking/pickup/proof is visible only to the owned order and client reload converges immediately.
tasks.action: Fix DSH state-machine/database owner first; update only exact partner/captain/control writer bindings and client projections required by the same transition.
mustNotChange: Do not make Partner/Captain a second order truth owner.
Do not expose location/proof outside owned-order scope.
Do not accept stale transition state/version silently.
Do not mark delivery/pickup complete optimistically before DSH commit.
acceptanceCriteria: Stale/forbidden transitions leave canonical state unchanged.
Location, pickup and proof remain object-scoped and privacy-safe.
Client/partner/captain/control readbacks converge on the same order version.
tasks.rollback: Revert the focused unit commit or roll forward at DSH while preserving audit/financial lineage; never restore a local order state machine.
tasks.commitBoundary: One state-machine/custody transition boundary with only directly affected writer/readback surfaces.

tasks.objective: Close cancellation, return, delivery exception and reassignment sagas without duplicate consequences
tasks.currentProblem: Cancellation/return/exception/reassignment can trigger dispatch and financial consequences; retry or stale state can otherwise create contradictory order truth or duplicate release/refund effects.
tasks.requiredChange: Trace cancellation/return/exception/reassignment through DSH order/dispatch sagas, outbox/correlation, database and WLT references. Repair legal transitions, idempotency, expected state/version, compensation/reconciliation and canonical client readback.
tasks.targetState: Each lifecycle exception reaches one auditable DSH terminal/intermediate truth; duplicate/retry is single-effect; required WLT consequence is correlated and WLT-owned; client sees the committed result or explicit pending/unknown state.
tasks.action: Repair DSH saga/state owner and WLT handoff first, then bounded operator/captain/partner writers and client readback.
mustNotChange: Do not double-release, double-refund or double-cancel on retry.
Do not conceal a pending/unknown financial consequence as complete.
Do not let a stale writer overwrite a newer order version.
Do not move refund/ledger truth into DSH.
acceptanceCriteria: Illegal/stale transitions fail without corrupting order state.
Financial consequence is one correlated WLT-owned effect or explicit unresolved state.
Client readback converges after compensation/reconciliation and does not fabricate completion.
tasks.rollback: Revert the focused unit commit or roll forward at DSH while preserving audit/financial lineage; never restore a local order state machine.
tasks.commitBoundary: Bounded exception/saga correction with WLT touch only for the same client-visible consequence.
